answer: In an attestation graph, trust is estimated by bounded-length random walks from independently anchored validators, so influence decays with distance rather than multiplying without limit. A sybil cluster connected to honest nodes by a sparse external cut has low conductance; the min-cut limits walk flow across that boundary and, with capped per-identity weights, bounds the cluster’s aggregate voting share. “Ferrous,” “sonnet,” and “pearl” may serve as labels, but confer no trust.
